questions.question: In accordance with Article 239AA of the Constitution of India, after the enforcement of the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991, the Union Territory of Delhi is designated by which of the following titles?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'National Capital Territory of Delhi'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Capital Territory of Delhi:**

 
 
• Article 239AA of the Constitution of India was inserted by the **Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991**.
 
• As per this article, the Union Territory of Delhi is formally designated as the **National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi**.
 
• The amendment provided for a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers for the NCT of Delhi.
 
• The Administrator of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, appointed under Article 239, is designated as the **Lieutenant Governor**.
 
• The Legislative Assembly has the power to make laws for the whole or any part of the NCT with respect to matters in the State List or Concurrent List, except for **Public Order, Police, and Land**.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Capital Region of Delhi:**

 
 
• The National Capital Region (NCR) is a unique multi-state regional planning area that encompasses the entire NCT of Delhi and several districts from neighboring states like Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
 
• While the NCT of Delhi is a constitutional administrative unit, the NCR is a broader planning region aimed at balanced development around the capital.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Capital of India:**
 
 
• While New Delhi serves as the seat of the Government of India and is effectively the administrative capital, this is a functional description rather than the formal constitutional title established by Article 239AA.
 
 
 
• **Union State of Delhi:**
 
 
• The term "Union State" is not a recognized constitutional category in India. India is a "Union of States," and Delhi is classified specifically as a Union Territory with special provisions, not a "Union State."
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The 69th Amendment Act came into force on **February 1, 1992**.
 
• The Legislative Assembly of Delhi consists of **70 members** chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies.
 
• The Council of Ministers consists of not more than **ten percent** of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly (i.e., a maximum of 7 ministers including the Chief Minister).
 
• The Chief Minister is appointed by the **President** (not the Lieutenant Governor), and other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Chief Minister.

questions.question: The length of each side of a rhombus is 17 cm and one of the diagonals is 30 cm. What is the area of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side = 17 cm, Half-diagonal (d₁/2) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

Using Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), the other half-diagonal = 8 cm.

Full second diagonal (d₂) = 8 × 2 = 16 cm.

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = (1/2) × 30 × 16.

Area = 15 × 16 = 240 cm².

**∴ Answer = 240 cm²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side (s) = 17 cm, One diagonal (d₁) = 30 cm

**Formula used:**

In a rhombus, s² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

 
 
• 
• Side = 17 15 15 8 8 Area = 1/2 × 30 × 16 = 240 cm²

**Calculations:**

Length of half of the given diagonal = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ Let the other half-diagonal be x.

⇒ 17² = 15² + x²

⇒ 289 = 225 + x²

⇒ x² = 289 − 225 = 64

⇒ x = √64 = 8 cm

⇒ Full second diagonal (d₂) = 8 × 2 = 16 cm

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 30 × 16

⇒ Area = 15 × 16 = 240 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 240 cm². (Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rhombus

Since all sides of a rhombus are equal, the perimeter is calculated as 4 × side.

Area via Base and Height

If the altitude (height) is known, the area can also be expressed as Base × Height.

Diagonal Property

The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular bisectors of each other and bisect the vertex angles.

Relation between Side and Diagonals

4 × s² = d₁² + d₂², where s is the side and d₁, d₂ are the diagonals.

 Total Sum = 540

questions.question: A trader marks his goods at a certain price and offers a 10% discount on it. In addition, he runs a scheme where for every 104 articles purchased, 16 articles are given free. If he still makes a profit of 17% on the overall transaction, find out by what percentage the marked price of an article is more than its cost price. Assume the customer pays for only 104 articles.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit multiplier = 1 + 17% = 1.17

Cash discount multiplier = 1 − 10% = 0.9

Free scheme multiplier = Articles Paid ÷ Total Articles = 104 ÷ (104 + 16) = 104/120 = 13/15

Markup Ratio (MP/CP) = Profit ÷ (Discount 1 × Discount 2)

Markup Ratio = 1.17 ÷ (0.9 × 13/15) = 1.17 ÷ (11.7/15) = 1.5

**∴ Answer = 50%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cash Discount = 10%, Free articles = 16 on 104 purchased, Overall Profit = 17%

**Formula used:**

Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

Total Revenue = Total Cost × (1 + Profit/100)

 
• CP (100) SP (117) MP (150) 
 
 Markup +50% 
 
 10% Disc. + 16 Free 
 
 Profit 17% 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1 article be 100.

⇒ Total articles given by trader = 104 + 16 = 120.

⇒ Total Cost = 120 × 100 = 12,000.

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) for 17% profit = 12,000 × 1.17 = 14,040.

⇒ This revenue is generated from 104 articles only. SP per article = 14,040 ÷ 104 = 135.

⇒ Since a 10% discount was offered on MP, 0.9 × MP = 135 ⇒ MP = 135 ÷ 0.9 = 150.

⇒ Markup % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP = (150 − 100) ÷ 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Cost Price Relation

The ratio of Marked Price (MP) to Cost Price (CP) is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Effective Discount on Free Items

When Y items are free on purchase of X items, the effective discount % = [Y / (X + Y)] × 100.

Successive Discount Formula

If two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given successively, the net discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂ / 100).

questions.question: With which State did the Department of Biotechnology sign the first Centre–State Memorandum of Understanding under the BioE3 Policy in 2025 to promote high-performance biomanufacturing?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Gujarat'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First Centre–State MoU under BioE3:**

 
 
• In early 2025, the **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)**, under the Ministry of Science and Technology, signed its first-ever Centre-State Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the **Government of Gujarat**.
 
• This landmark agreement was established to implement the **BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment, and Employment) Policy**, specifically focusing on high-performance biomanufacturing.
 
• The partnership aims to leverage Gujarat's robust industrial infrastructure, particularly in chemicals and pharmaceuticals, to transition towards sustainable, bio-based manufacturing processes.
 
• The MoU facilitates the setting up of specialized **biomanufacturing hubs** and bio-foundries in the state, which are essential for scaling up laboratory-level biotechnological innovations to industrial production.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu:**

 
 
• Tamil Nadu is a leader in the pharmaceutical and medical device sectors in India. While the state is actively pursuing biotechnology initiatives and has several biotech parks, it was not the first state to sign the specific BioE3 MoU in 2025.
 
 
 
• **Assam:**
 
 
• Assam is recognized for its rich biodiversity and potential in bio-resources. The government has been promoting the "Bio-Tech Vision," but its primary focus remains on bio-resource utilization rather than being the pioneer for the national high-performance biomanufacturing MoU under BioE3.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka:**
 
 
• Often referred to as the "Biotech Capital of India," Karnataka hosts a significant percentage of India's biotech companies. Despite its dominance in the sector, the first formal Centre-State collaboration specifically for the 2025 BioE3 high-performance biomanufacturing framework was initiated with Gujarat.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The **BioE3 Policy** was approved by the Union Cabinet to foster a high-performance biomanufacturing ecosystem in India, aiming to address climate change and promote a circular bioeconomy.
 
• The policy focuses on six thematic areas: **Bio-based chemicals and enzymes, functional foods and smart proteins, precision biotherapeutics, climate-resilient agriculture, carbon capture and utilization, and futuristic marine and space research.**
 
• High-performance biomanufacturing is expected to play a crucial role in India's goal of reaching a **$300 billion bio-economy by 2030**.
 
• The initiative encourages "integrated" science where the Centre and States work together to bridge the gap between discovery-to-innovation and innovation-to-commercialization.

questions.question: Evaluate: 16 + 20 ÷ 5 - 2 × 4
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply BODMAS rule order: Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

Divide: 20 ÷ 5 = 4

Multiply: 2 × 4 = 8

Calculate: 16 + 4 − 8 = 12

**∴ Answer = 12**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 16 + 20 ÷ 5 − 2 × 4

**Formula used:**

BODMAS Rule: B (Brackets), O (Of), D (Division), M (Multiplication), A (Addition), S (Subtraction).

 20 ÷ 5 = 4 2 × 4 = 8 
• 
• 16 + 4 − 8 
• 12 

**Calculations:**

The expression is 16 + 20 ÷ 5 − 2 × 4

⇒ 16 + 4 − 2 × 4 (After Division: 20 ÷ 5 = 4)

⇒ 16 + 4 − 8 (After Multiplication: 2 × 4 = 8)

⇒ 20 − 8 (After Addition: 16 + 4 = 20)

⇒ 12 (After Subtraction: 20 − 8 = 12)

**∴ The correct answer is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

It stands for Viniculum (bar), Brackets (), Of (×), Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Division and Multiplication Priority

Division and Multiplication have equal priority and are solved from left to right if they appear consecutively in an expression.

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Similarly, Addition and Subtraction have equal priority and are generally solved from left to right once higher-order operations are completed.

questions.question: What is the primary pigment responsible for photosynthesis in plants?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Chlorophyll'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorophyll:**

 
 
• Chlorophyll is the primary pigment used by plants, algae, and cyanobacteria to absorb light energy for photosynthesis.
 
• It is located within the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplasts, which are specialized organelles in plant cells.
 
• There are several types of chlorophyll, with **Chlorophyll-a** and **Chlorophyll-b** being the most common in terrestrial plants. Chlorophyll-a is specifically responsible for the light-dependent reactions.
 
• Chlorophyll absorbs light most efficiently in the blue-violet and red parts of the electromagnetic spectrum, while it reflects green light, which is why plants appear green to the human eye.
 
• The molecule has a porphyrin ring structure with a **magnesium atom** at its center, which is crucial for the absorption of light energy and the subsequent excitation of electrons.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carotenoid:**

 
 
• Carotenoids are accessory pigments that are typically yellow, orange, or red. They assist in photosynthesis by absorbing wavelengths of light that chlorophyll cannot.
 
• They play a vital role in **photoprotection**, where they dissipate excess light energy that could otherwise damage the chlorophyll molecule or the plant tissue.
 
 
 
• **Xanthophyll:**
 
 
• Xanthophylls are a specific class of carotenoids that contain oxygen in their molecular structure.
 
• They primarily produce yellow hues and function alongside other pigments to harvest light energy and protect the plant from high light intensity via the xanthophyll cycle.
 
 
 
• **Anthocyanin:**
 
 
• Anthocyanins are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that can appear red, purple, or blue depending on the pH level.
 
• Unlike chlorophyll or carotenoids, anthocyanins are **not involved in the process of photosynthesis**. Instead, they serve to attract pollinators, protect plants against cold stress, and act as antioxidants.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The process of photosynthesis converts solar energy into chemical energy (glucose), providing the foundation for most food chains on Earth.
 
• The primary site of photosynthesis in most plants is the **mesophyll layer** of the leaves.
 
• In autumn, as chlorophyll breaks down due to shorter days and cooler temperatures, the underlying accessory pigments like carotenoids and xanthophylls become visible, leading to the changing colors of leaves.
 
• The absorption spectrum of chlorophyll is a key factor in determining the **Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR)**, which is the range of light (400 to 700 nanometers) that organisms use for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following programmes aims to increase soil fertility and thereby helps in production of healthy food through organic practices without the use of agro-chemicals?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY):**

 
 
• PKVY is a sub-component of the Soil Health Management (SHM) scheme under the National Mission of Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), launched in 2015.
 
• The primary objective of this programme is to support and promote organic farming, which results in the improvement of soil health and fertility.
 
• It encourages the production of agricultural products free from chemicals and pesticide residues by adopting eco-friendly, low-cost technologies.
 
• The scheme is implemented via a cluster approach, where groups of farmers are encouraged to take up organic farming through the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) for certification.
 
• It aims to provide institutional support and handholding for farmers to transition from conventional farming to organic farming, ensuring a better market for their produce.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan MaanDhan Yojana (PMKMY):**

 
 
• This is a government-backed pension scheme specifically designed for small and marginal farmers (SMFs) in India.
 
• It provides a monthly pension of ₹3,000 to eligible farmers after they reach the age of 60, acting as a social security net.
 
• It is a voluntary and contributory scheme where the farmer and the Central Government contribute an equal amount to the pension fund.
 
 
 
• **Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY):**
 
 
• Launched in 2007, this umbrella scheme aims at the holistic development of agriculture and allied sectors.
 
• It provides states with the flexibility and autonomy to plan and execute agricultural development programmes based on their local needs and agro-climatic conditions.
 
• The scheme focuses on increasing public investment in agriculture and achieving a higher growth rate in the sector through infrastructure development and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):**
 
 
• PMFBY is a crop insurance scheme launched in 2016 to provide financial support to farmers suffering from crop loss or damage arising out of unforeseen events.
 
• It covers all food and oilseed crops and annual commercial/horticultural crops against natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
 
• The scheme aims to stabilize the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming and encourage them to adopt innovative agricultural practices.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The financial assistance under PKVY is provided for a 3-year period to clusters of farmers for various activities like mobilization, organic seeds, harvesting, and branding.
 
• Under the cluster approach, a minimum of 50 or more farmers form a cluster having 50 acres of land to take up organic farming.
 
• The **Participatory Guarantee System (PGS)** is a key element of PKVY, which is a process of certifying organic products that ensures they adhere to quality standards without the high cost of third-party certification.
 
• Promotion of organic farming under this scheme also helps in carbon sequestration and mitigating the ill effects of climate change on Indian agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics represents the ability of a computer to work continuously without fatigue?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Diligence'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diligence:**

 
 
• Diligence refers to the capacity of a computer to perform repetitive tasks for long periods without getting tired, bored, or losing concentration.
 
• Unlike human beings, who may experience physical fatigue or mental exhaustion after working for several hours, a computer can work for days without any break and still maintain the same level of performance.
 
• Even if millions of calculations are performed, a computer will complete the last calculation with the same accuracy and speed as the first one.
 
• This characteristic makes computers ideal for industrial automation, data processing, and complex scientific simulations that require continuous operation.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Versatility:**

 
 
• Versatility is the ability of a computer to perform completely different types of work at the same time or in quick succession.
 
• For example, a computer can be used to prepare a payroll slip, while simultaneously playing music in the background and downloading a file from the internet.
 
• This flexibility allows computers to be used in various fields, such as education, medicine, business, and entertainment.
 
 
 
• **Accuracy:**
 
 
• Accuracy refers to the degree of correctness with which a computer performs its operations.
 
• Computers are highly accurate and perform every calculation with the same precision. Errors in computing are usually not caused by the machine but by incorrect data input or faulty programming, a concept known as GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out).
 
 
 
• **Speed:**
 
 
• Speed is the capability of a computer to process data and execute instructions at an incredibly fast rate.
 
• Modern computers can perform millions or even billions of instructions per second (MIPS or BIPS). Tasks that would take a human years to complete can be finished by a computer in a few seconds.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• While computers possess many advantages over humans, they lack **IQ (Intelligence Quotient)**. A computer cannot take its own decisions and follows only the instructions provided by the user.
 
• Another limitation is **No Feeling**; computers do not have emotions, taste, or intuition, which prevents them from making value-based judgments.
 
• **Storage (Memory):** A computer has an in-built memory where it can store a vast amount of data. This data can be retrieved instantaneously whenever required.
 
• The physical components of a computer are referred to as **Hardware**, while the set of instructions that tell the hardware what to do is called **Software**.

questions.question: In 2025, which state had One-Stop Centres that assisted approximately 2.39 lakh women?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Uttar Pradesh'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uttar Pradesh and One-Stop Centres:**

 
 
• Uttar Pradesh has emerged as the leading state in providing assistance to women through the One-Stop Centre (OSC) scheme, reaching a milestone of assisting approximately **2.39 lakh women** by recent assessment periods leading into 2025.
 
• The state has effectively implemented these centres across various districts to provide integrated support to women affected by violence, both in private and public spaces.
 
• The high number of beneficiaries in Uttar Pradesh is attributed to the extensive outreach programs, the dense population, and the proactive administrative measures taken to ensure that the services of the 'Sakhi' centres reach the grassroots level.
 
• These centres in the state provide a range of services under one roof, including medical aid, police facilitation, legal counseling, and temporary shelter.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gujarat:**

 
 
• Gujarat has a well-established network of One-Stop Centres and has integrated them with its existing women's helpline services (181 Abhayam).
 
• While the state has been successful in resolving thousands of cases, the total volume of women assisted at these specific centres does not match the 2.39 lakh figure associated with Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra:**
 
 
• Maharashtra operates numerous One-Stop Centres and has its own state-specific schemes like 'Manodhairya' to support victims of violence.
 
• Although the state provides comprehensive support, its recorded numbers for assisted women in the OSC framework are significant but lower than the specific statistics reported for Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar has been progressively establishing OSCs in all its districts to address gender-based violence and provide social and legal support.
 
• While Bihar has shown improvement in the utilization of these centres, the scale of outreach and the documented number of beneficiaries have not yet reached the 2.39 lakh mark as of the current reporting cycle.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The **One-Stop Centre (OSC) Scheme**, popularly known as **'Sakhi'**, was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) on **April 1, 2015**.
 
• It is a **centrally sponsored scheme** funded through the **Nirbhaya Fund**, aimed at supporting women affected by violence in any form (domestic, sexual harassment, etc.).
 
• The primary objective is to provide **24x7 emergency response** and support services, including specialized medical and psychological assistance.
 
• Nationwide, over 700 One-Stop Centres have been approved, with Uttar Pradesh hosting a significant portion of these to cater to its large population.

questions.question: Which amendment to the Indian constitution provided a special status to the Union Territory of Delhi, and redesignated it the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is '69th Constitutional Amendment'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991:**

 
 
• The 69th Amendment Act of 1991 provided a special status to the Union Territory of Delhi and redesignated it as the **National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi**.
 
• This amendment inserted **Articles 239AA and 239AB** into the Indian Constitution.
 
• It created a **Legislative Assembly** for Delhi and a Council of Ministers headed by a Chief Minister.
 
• The Legislative Assembly was given the power to make laws on subjects in the State List (except police, public order, and land) and the Concurrent List.
 
• The administrator of the NCT of Delhi was designated as the **Lieutenant Governor (L-G)**.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **68th Constitutional Amendment:**

 
 
• Passed in 1991, this amendment was specifically concerned with the state of **Punjab**.
 
• It amended Article 356 to allow the extension of **President's Rule** in Punjab for a total period of five years due to the internal disturbance in the state at that time.
 
 
 
• **70th Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• Passed in 1992, this amendment focused on the **Presidential elections**.
 
• It provided for the inclusion of the members of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of **Delhi** and the Union Territory of **Pondicherry** (now Puducherry) in the Electoral College for the election of the President of India.
 
 
 
• **71st Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• Passed in 1992, this amendment dealt with the **languages** of India.
 
• It amended the **Eighth Schedule** of the Constitution to include three more languages: **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali**. This increased the total number of languages in the Eighth Schedule to 18 at that time.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The 69th Amendment was based on the recommendations of the **S. Balakrishnan Committee**, which examined the issues relating to the administration of Delhi.
 
• While Delhi has a Legislative Assembly, it remains a **Union Territory**, which often leads to complex jurisdictional dynamics between the elected government and the Central Government (via the Lieutenant Governor).
 
• The amendment came into force on **February 1, 1992**.
 
• The strength of the Council of Ministers for Delhi was fixed at **ten percent** of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly (i.e., 7 ministers for a 70-member assembly).

questions.question: What is a significant feature of Indian architecture related to caves?

options.text: Excavation of caves for religious purposes

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Excavation of caves for religious purposes'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excavation of caves for religious purposes:**

 
 
• Cave architecture, also known as rock-cut architecture, is one of the most spectacular features of ancient Indian heritage, where structures were created by carving out solid natural rock.
 
• In India, these caves were primarily excavated to serve as religious retreats, prayer halls (Chaityas), and monasteries (Viharas) for monks and devotees.
 
• The practice began around the 3rd century BCE, initially associated with Buddhism and Jainism, and later with Hinduism.
 
• Architects and sculptors displayed immense skill by carving intricate pillars, statues of deities, and decorative facades directly into mountainsides, ensuring the structures would last for centuries.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Influence of European architecture:**

 
 
• European architectural influence in India (such as Gothic, Neo-Classical, and Baroque styles) emerged much later, during the colonial period starting in the 16th century.
 
• Common examples include the Victoria Memorial and various churches in Goa, which are distinct from the ancient tradition of rock-cut cave architecture.
 
 
 
• **Development of skyscrapers:**
 
 
• The development of skyscrapers is a modern architectural phenomenon driven by 20th and 21st-century engineering, steel frames, and urban density.
 
• Ancient Indian cave architecture focused on subterranean or mountain-embedded structures rather than vertical, multi-story buildings constructed from the ground up.
 
 
 
• **Use of marble in construction:**
 
 
• While marble became a defining material in Indian architecture, it is most famously associated with the Indo-Islamic and Mughal periods (e.g., the Taj Mahal).
 
• Ancient cave excavations were predominantly carved out of hard volcanic basalt (as in the Deccan) or granite, rather than being built using marble slabs.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The earliest examples of rock-cut architecture in India are the **Barabar Caves** in Bihar, dating back to the Mauryan Empire (3rd century BCE).
 
• The **Ajanta Caves** (Maharashtra) are world-renowned for their Buddhist paintings and sculptures, while the **Ellora Caves** are famous for the monolithic **Kailasa Temple**.
 
• These caves demonstrate a transition from wood-based structures to permanent stone excavations, often mimicking the wooden carpentry of that era in stone details.
 
• Most of these sites were located along ancient trade routes, allowing them to serve as resting places for travelling merchants and monks alike.

questions.question: Which irrigation method delivers water directly to roots using emitters for optimal moisture control and efficiency?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Drip'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drip Irrigation:**

 
 
• Drip irrigation, also known as trickle irrigation, is a micro-irrigation system that saves water and nutrients by allowing water to drip slowly to the roots of plants.
 
• The goal is to place water directly into the root zone and minimize evaporation through a network of valves, pipes, tubing, and emitters.
 
• It is considered the most water-efficient method of irrigation, often reaching efficiency levels of over 90% because it reduces runoff and deep percolation.
 
• This method is highly effective for row crops, orchards, and greenhouses where precise moisture control is required to enhance crop yield and quality.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overhead Irrigation:**

 
 
• This method involves distributing water through high-pressure sprinklers or guns from a central location in the field or from moving platforms.
 
• While effective for large areas, it is less efficient than drip irrigation due to high evaporation rates and the potential for water to be diverted by wind.
 
 
 
• **Flood Irrigation:**
 
 
• Flood irrigation is an ancient method where water is pumped or brought to the fields and allowed to flow over the ground among the crops.
 
• It is generally the least efficient method as a large amount of water is lost to evaporation, runoff, and infiltration below the root zone.
 
• It can also lead to soil erosion and waterlogging if not managed properly.
 
 
 
• **Sprinkler Irrigation:**
 
 
• In this method, water is sprayed into the air through sprinklers so that it falls on the ground surface somewhat like rainfall.
 
• The spray is developed by the flow of water under pressure through small orifices or nozzles.
 
• While more controlled than flood irrigation, it still suffers from water loss due to evaporation and can promote the growth of fungi on wet leaves.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• Modern drip irrigation was popularized by **Simcha Blass** and his son Yeshayahu in Israel during the 1960s.
 
• One of the major advantages of drip irrigation is **fertigation**, which is the application of water-soluble fertilizers directly through the irrigation system to the plant roots.
 
• This system significantly reduces weed growth because water is only applied where the crop is growing, leaving the gaps between rows dry.
 
• Drip irrigation is particularly vital in arid and semi-arid regions where water scarcity is a major constraint on agricultural productivity.

When partners invest their capital for different time periods, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of their capital and time period (Capital₁ × Time₁ : Capital₂ × Time₂).

Simple Partnership

questions.question: Two people, A and B, start running from the same point on a circular track of length 400 meters, but in opposite directions. A runs at 6 m/s and B at 4 m/s. In how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For meeting in opposite directions, use Relative Speed = Sum of individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 6 + 4 = 10 m/s.

Time to meet for the first time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed.

Time = 400 ÷ 10 = 40 seconds.

**∴ Answer = 40 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of circular track = 400 meters

Speed of A = 6 m/s, Speed of B = 4 m/s

Direction of running = Opposite

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = SpeedA + SpeedB

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 Start Point 
 A (6 m/s) 
 B (4 m/s) Track = 400 m Relative Speed = 6 + 4 = 10 m/s 

**Calculations:**

Since both move in opposite directions, the distance between them reduces by the sum of their speeds every second.

⇒ Relative Speed = 6 + 4 = 10 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet for the first time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 400 ÷ 10 = 40 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 40 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same Direction Meeting Time

If two people run in the same direction, the time to meet for the first time is Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ − Speed₂).

Meeting at Starting Point

The time they will meet at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one full lap: LCM(L/S₁, L/S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If speeds are in simplified ratio a:b, they meet at (a + b) distinct points when moving in opposite directions, and |a − b| distinct points when moving in the same direction.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is India’s nearest neighbour in the northwest?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Pakistan'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pakistan:**

 
 
• Pakistan is India's immediate neighbor located to the **northwest** of the Indian mainland.
 
• The boundary between India and Pakistan was demarcated in 1947 and is known as the **Radcliffe Line**.
 
• India shares a land border of approximately **3,323 km** with Pakistan, which is one of the most significant and sensitive borders in the world.
 
• The Indian states and Union Territories that share a border with Pakistan are **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir, and Ladakh**.
 
• Geographically, the northwestern region transitions from the fertile plains of Punjab to the Thar Desert in Rajasthan and the marshy Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nepal:**

 
 
• Nepal is located to the **north** of India, nestled in the central Himalayas.
 
• It is a landlocked country that shares borders with five Indian states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Sikkim.
 
• India and Nepal share an "open border," allowing citizens of both countries to move freely across it without passports or visas for various purposes.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan:**
 
 
• Bhutan is a landlocked country situated in the Eastern Himalayas, to the **north/northeast** of India.
 
• It shares borders with the Indian states of Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• India and Bhutan maintain a very close relationship, particularly in areas of hydropower, trade, and defense.
 
 
 
• **China:**
 
 
• China is India's largest neighbor to the **north**.
 
• The border between India and China is often divided into three sectors: the Western sector (Ladakh), the Middle sector (Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand), and the Eastern sector (Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh).
 
• The border in the eastern sector is known as the **McMahon Line**, while the de facto border in other regions is referred to as the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• India has a total land frontier of about **15,106.7 km** and a coastline of **7,516.6 km** including island territories.
 
• Apart from Pakistan, **Afghanistan** is also considered a neighbor in the northwest, sharing a small border (approx. 106 km) with the Union Territory of Ladakh (currently in the POK region).
 
• India shares its longest land border with **Bangladesh** (4,096.7 km) and its shortest with **Afghanistan**.
 
• To the south, India's nearest island neighbors are **Sri Lanka** and **Maldives**.

72 is related to 22 following a certain logic. Following the same logic,132 is related to 37. To which of the following is 108 related, following the same logic?

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the Indian National Congress’s stance on communal politics during the Moderate phase?

options.text: Accepted political demands based on religious identities
Maintained a secular approach in its programmes and demands
Aligned itself with leaders of specific religious communities
Limited organisational participation to a single religious group

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Maintained a secular approach in its programmes and demands'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secular Approach of the Moderates:**

 
 
• During the Moderate phase (1885–1905), the Indian National Congress (INC) was deeply committed to the idea of a secular nation. They believed that the political and economic interests of Indians were common, regardless of their religious affiliations.
 
• The Moderates made conscious efforts to avoid any demands or actions that could be seen as favoring one religious community over another, aiming to build a broad-based national unity against British colonial rule.
 
• They functioned on the principle that religion is a private matter and should not interfere with the political struggle for constitutional reforms and civil liberties.
 
• To ensure the participation of all communities, the Congress passed a rule in 1888 stating that no resolution would be passed if an overwhelming majority of Hindu or Muslim delegates objected to it.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Demands Based on Religious Identities:**

 
 
• The INC, in its early years, strictly rejected political demands based on religious identities. They viewed communal demands as a threat to the emerging Indian nationalism.
 
• The British later encouraged communal demands (like the demand for separate electorates) to implement their 'Divide and Rule' policy, but the Moderates resisted this by focusing on universal economic and political grievances.
 
 
 
• **Alignment with Specific Religious Leaders:**
 
 
• While the INC included leaders from various religions (such as Dadabhai Naoroji, Badruddin Tyabji, and Pherozeshah Mehta), they did not align with leaders who promoted communalism or exclusive religious interests.
 
• The goal was to present a united front of Indian citizens rather than a federation of religious groups.
 
 
 
• **Organisational Participation:**
 
 
• The INC was never limited to a single religious group. From its very first session in 1885, it invited delegates from all parts of India and all walks of life.
 
• The election of Badruddin Tyabji as the first Muslim President of the INC in 1887 was a clear message that the organization was inclusive and represented all Indians.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The **Moderate Phase** of the Indian National Congress lasted from **1885 to 1905**.
 
• Prominent leaders of this phase included **W.C. Bonnerjee, Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, and Surendranath Banerjee**.
 
• Their primary methods were **Prayers, Petitions, and Protests (3Ps)** within the framework of the law, aiming for gradual constitutional reforms.
 
• The Moderates were successful in creating a sense of Indian "nationhood" and exposing the exploitative nature of British economic policies through the **"Drain of Wealth"** theory.
 
• Despite their secular stance, the British attempted to alienate the Muslim community from the Congress, eventually leading to the formation of the All India Muslim League in 1906.

questions.question: Article 47 deals with which of the following?

options.text: Raising the level of nutrition and public health

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Raising the level of nutrition and public health'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 47:**

 
 
• Article 47 of the Indian Constitution falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It states that the State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties.
 
• The article also mandates that the State shall endeavor to bring about prohibition of the consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health.
 
• This article is classified under the Socialist principles as it aims to provide social justice and improve the welfare of the people.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Participation of workers in management:**

 
 
• This is covered under **Article 43A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• It directs the State to take steps, by suitable legislation or in any other way, to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments, or other organizations engaged in any industry.
 
 
 
• **Protection of environment:**
 
 
• This is covered under **Article 48A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, it states that the State shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country.
 
 
 
• **Organization of agriculture:**
 
 
• This is covered under **Article 48** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and, in particular, take steps for preserving and improving the breeds, and prohibiting the slaughter of cows and calves and other milch and draught cattle.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are enumerated in **Part IV** of the Constitution from **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• The framers of the Constitution borrowed this idea from the **Irish Constitution** of 1937, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
 
• The DPSPs are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• However, Article 37 itself says that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• The Directive Principles can be classified into three broad categories: **Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-intellectual**.

questions.question: Which of the following freedom fighters led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'B R Ambedkar'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **B R Ambedkar and the Mahad Satyagraha:**

 
 
• The Mahad Satyagraha was led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on March 20, 1927, in Mahad, Maharashtra.
 
• The primary objective of this movement was to assert the right of the Dalits (then referred to as untouchables) to use water from the public Chavdar Tank, which they were previously forbidden from accessing.
 
• This event is considered a foundational moment in the Dalit movement in India, as it challenged the centuries-old caste-based discrimination and the practice of untouchability.
 
• Ambedkar argued that the Satyagraha was not just about water, but about establishing the fundamental human equality of all people.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jyotirao Phule:**

 
 
• Jyotirao Phule was a prominent 19th-century social reformer from Maharashtra who founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society).
 
• He worked extensively for the education of women and the lower castes; however, he passed away in 1890, decades before the Mahad Satyagraha occurred.
 
 
 
• **E V Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar):**
 
 
• E.V. Ramaswamy, commonly known as Periyar, was the father of the Self-Respect Movement in South India.
 
• While he was a staunch advocate against caste discrimination and participated in the Vaikom Satyagraha in Kerala, he was not the leader of the Mahad Satyagraha in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **K Kelappan:**
 
 
• K. Kelappan, often called the "Kerala Gandhi," was a celebrated freedom fighter and social reformer from Kerala.
 
• He was instrumental in the Vaikom Satyagraha and the Guruvayur Satyagraha, which focused on temple entry rights in the Malabar region, rather than the Mahad water rights movement.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• During the second phase of the Mahad Satyagraha in December 1927, Dr. Ambedkar and his followers publicly burned the **Manusmriti** to protest against the religious basis of caste-based inequality.
 
• In India, March 20 is often observed as **Social Empowerment Day** (Samajik Sadbhavna Diwas) to commemorate the Mahad Satyagraha.
 
• The Satyagraha was a response to the Mahad Municipality's failure to implement a 1923 resolution (the Bole Resolution) that allowed untouchables to use public places and water bodies.
 
• The legal battle for the Chavdar Tank continued for years, eventually resulting in a victory in the Bombay High Court in 1937, affirming the right of Dalits to use the tank.

questions.question: Which technique was primarily used to produce flake tools in India during the Middle Palaeolithic culture?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Levallois technique'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Levallois Technique:**

 
 
• The Levallois technique is a distinctive type of stone-knapping developed by precursors to modern humans during the Palaeolithic period. It is the defining technological hallmark of the Middle Palaeolithic culture in India.
 
• This technique involves the **preparation of a stone core** by striking pieces off the edges until it acquires a specific shape (often compared to a tortoise shell).
 
• Once the core is prepared, a final "predetermined" flake is struck off. This allowed the tool-maker to have much greater control over the size and shape of the resulting flake tool.
 
• In the Indian context, the Middle Palaeolithic is often referred to as the **"Nevasan" culture** (named after the site of Nevasa), where flake tools produced using this method became dominant over the heavy handaxes of the preceding era.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the actual population growth?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Urbanisation rate'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Actual Population Growth:**

 
 
• Actual population growth is the change in the number of inhabitants of a territory during a specific period of time, accounting for both natural changes and movement of people.
 
• It is calculated using four primary components: Births, Deaths, In-migration (Immigration), and Out-migration (Emigration).
 
• The formula for actual growth is: (Births - Deaths) + (In-migration - Out-migration).
 
• Unlike natural growth, which only considers births and deaths, actual growth provides a comprehensive view of how a population size changes due to all demographic factors.
 
 
 
• **Urbanisation Rate:**
 
 
• The urbanisation rate refers to the percentage of the total population living in urban areas or the rate at which the proportion of the urban population is increasing.
 
• While urbanisation is a significant demographic process, it describes the **distribution** and **concentration** of people rather than a direct component used to calculate the numerical increase or decrease of the total population.
 
• Therefore, it is a measure of settlement patterns, not a component of the actual growth calculation.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Birth Rate:**

 
 
• The Crude Birth Rate (CBR) is expressed as the number of live births in a year per thousand of the population.
 
• It is a fundamental "positive" component of population growth as it adds individuals to the total count.
 
 
 
• **Death Rate:**
 
 
• The Crude Death Rate (CDR) is the number of deaths in a particular year per thousand of the population in a particular area.
 
• It plays a vital role in population change; population growth occurs not just by increasing the birth rate but also by decreasing the death rate.
 
 
 
• **In-migration:**
 
 
• In-migration or Immigration refers to the movement of people into a new area or country to settle there permanently or semi-permanently.
 
• This is a crucial component of actual population growth because it increases the population of the destination area, independent of the local birth and death rates.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Natural Growth:** This is the difference between births and deaths in a specific region between two points in time. Formula: Births - Deaths.
 
• **Migration:** This is the movement of people across territories. It can be internal (within a country) or international.
 
• While internal migration (rural to urban) drives the **urbanisation rate**, it does not change the total actual population of the country; it only redistributes it.
 
• The net effect of migration (In-migration minus Out-migration) is what determines the "Migration" component of actual growth.

questions.question: Which of the following plant tissues is NOT a type of simple tissue?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Xylem'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem:**

 
 
• Xylem is classified as a **complex permanent tissue** rather than a simple tissue because it consists of more than one type of cell that works together as a unit.
 
• It is responsible for the conduction of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Xylem is composed of four distinct types of elements: **tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres**.
 
• Except for xylem parenchyma, all other xylem elements are dead cells at maturity and have thick lignified walls, which also provide mechanical strength to the plant body.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• Parenchyma is a **simple permanent tissue** made of relatively unspecialized cells with thin cell walls.
 
• The cells are usually living and have large intercellular spaces; they are primarily involved in food storage and photosynthesis (chlorenchyma).
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• Collenchyma is a **simple permanent tissue** that provides flexibility and mechanical support to young plant parts like stems and petioles.
 
• The cells are living, elongated, and irregularly thickened at the corners with cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
 
• It allows easy bending in various parts of a plant without breaking.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma:**
 
 
• Sclerenchyma is a **simple permanent tissue** that makes the plant hard and stiff (e.g., the husk of a coconut).
 
• The cells of this tissue are dead, long, and narrow with walls greatly thickened due to **lignin** deposition.
 
• These walls are often so thick that there is no internal space inside the cell.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• Plant tissues are broadly divided into two main groups: **Meristematic tissue** (cells capable of division) and **Permanent tissue** (cells that have lost the ability to divide).
 
• Permanent tissues are further categorized into:
 
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue:** Composed of cells that are structurally and functionally similar (Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma).
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissue:** Composed of more than one type of cell working together to perform a common function (Xylem and Phloem).
 
 
 
• **Phloem** is the other complex tissue which transports food materials, usually from leaves to other parts of the plant, and consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 32 hours respectively. A third tap can empty it in 4 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?

Since Tap 1 (4h) and Tap 3 (4h) have the same rate, they cancel each other out.

Net filling rate = Efficiency of Tap 2 = 1/32 of cistern per hour.

Time to fill full cistern = 32 hours.

**∴ Answer = 8**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

questions.question: A frequency distribution has a mean of 55 and a mode of 50. If the empirical relation holds, what should be the median of the data set? (Round off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the empirical relationship: 3 × Median = Mode + 2 × Mean.

3 × Median = 50 + 2 × 55

3 × Median = 50 + 110 = 160

Median = 160 ÷ 3 = 53.333...

**∴ Answer = 53.33**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean = 55, Mode = 50

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean (Empirical Relation)

 Frequency Distribution (Positive Skew) 
 
• Mode = 50 
• Median = 53.33 
• Mean = 55 
• 

**Calculations:**

Substitute the given values into the empirical formula:

⇒ 50 = 3 × Median − 2 × 55

⇒ 50 = 3 × Median − 110

⇒ 50 + 110 = 3 × Median

⇒ 160 = 3 × Median

⇒ Median = 160 ÷ 3

⇒ Median ≈ 53.333...

**∴ The correct answer is 53.33 (Option 2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Karl Pearson's Empirical Relation

For moderately skewed distributions, the distance between the mean and the median is approximately one-third of the distance between the mean and the mode: (Mean − Mode) = 3 × (Mean − Median).

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical bell-shaped distribution (like the normal distribution), the three measures of central tendency coincide: Mean = Median = Mode.

Skewness and Values

In a positively skewed distribution, Mean > Median > Mode. In a negatively skewed distribution, Mode > Median > Mean.

Standard Error of Median

questions.question: What was the name given to the special officials appointed by Ashoka to spread his policy of Dhamma?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Dhamma Mahamatta'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhamma Mahamatta:**

 
 
• Dhamma Mahamattas were a special class of officers established by the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka to spread and enforce his policy of Dhamma (Dharma).
 
• According to Ashoka's inscriptions, specifically Major Rock Edict V, these officials were appointed in the 13th year of his reign.
 
• Their primary responsibility was to look after the spiritual and moral well-being of the subjects and to propagate the principles of Dhamma across the vast Mauryan Empire.
 
• They were tasked with promoting harmony among different religious sects, including Brahmanas, Ajivikas, and Buddhists, and were also involved in charitable activities and the welfare of prisoners.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dhamma Lekhakas:**

 
 
• The term 'Lekhaka' generally refers to a scribe or a writer in ancient Indian administration.
 
• While Ashoka employed many scribes to engrave his edicts on rocks and pillars, there was no specific official designation called "Dhamma Lekhakas" used for the moral propagation of his policy.
 
 
 
• **Dhamma Janapada:**
 
 
• The word 'Janapada' refers to the land, territory, or a realm of a tribe or people in ancient India.
 
• While Ashoka focused on the welfare of the people in various Janapadas, this term does not refer to an official post or person responsible for spreading Dhamma.
 
 
 
• **Dhamma Mukhyas:**
 
 
• 'Mukhya' translates to a chief or a head of a village or organization.
 
• Although administrative heads existed at various levels of the Mauryan bureaucracy, "Dhamma Mukhyas" was not the formal title used in the Ashokan edicts for the officials designated to spread the Dhamma.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• Ashoka was the first king in Indian history who left his records engraved on stones and pillars.
 
• The policy of **Dhamma** was not a new religion but a code of social and ethical conduct intended to maintain peace and order in a diverse society.
 
• Other officials like the **Rajukas** (judicial/land measurement officers) and **Yuktas** (secretaries/accountants) were also commanded by Ashoka to propagate the principles of Dhamma during their official tours.
 
• Ashoka even sent his son, **Mahendra**, and daughter, **Sanghamitra**, to Sri Lanka to spread the message of Buddhism and Dhamma.
 
• The Major Rock Edicts and Pillar Edicts serve as the primary source of information regarding the appointment and duties of the **Dhamma Mahamattas**.

questions.question: The energy stored in human liver and muscle tissues is mainly in the form of which carbohydrate?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Glycogen'**

Carbohydrates are the primary source of energy for the human body. When we consume more glucose than the body needs for immediate energy, the excess is converted into a storage form to be used later during periods of fasting or intense physical activity.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glycogen:**

 
 
• Glycogen is a large, branched polysaccharide that serves as the main storage form of glucose in humans and animals.
 
• It is primarily synthesized and stored in the **liver** and the **skeletal muscles**.
 
• The process of converting glucose into glycogen is known as **glycogenesis**, which occurs when blood sugar levels are high (usually after eating).
 
• Muscle glycogen provides a readily available source of energy for the muscle cells themselves during exercise, while liver glycogen is broken down into glucose and released into the bloodstream to maintain blood sugar levels for the entire body, especially the brain.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Starch:**

 
 
• Starch is the primary storage carbohydrate in **plants**. It consists of two types of molecules: amylose and amylopectin.
 
• While it is a major part of the human diet (found in potatoes, rice, and wheat), humans do not store energy as starch; they digest it into glucose and then store it as glycogen.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose:**
 
 
• Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide found in the **cell walls of plants**.
 
• It provides rigidity and strength to plants. Humans lack the enzymes (cellulase) necessary to digest cellulose, so it passes through the digestive tract as dietary fiber.
 
 
 
• **Sucrose:**
 
 
• Sucrose is a disaccharide commonly known as **table sugar**, composed of one glucose molecule and one fructose molecule.
 
• It is naturally found in many plants, such as sugar cane and sugar beets, but it is not a storage form of energy within human tissues.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The regulation of glycogen is controlled by hormones: **Insulin** promotes the storage of glucose as glycogen, while **Glucagon** (and Adrenaline) triggers the breakdown of glycogen into glucose when energy is needed.
 
• The total amount of glycogen stored in the body is limited; once glycogen stores are full, excess glucose is typically converted into **fat (triglycerides)** and stored in adipose tissue.
 
• Liver glycogen typically accounts for about 5-10% of the liver's weight, whereas muscle glycogen accounts for about 1-2% of muscle weight. However, because humans have more muscle mass than liver mass, the total amount of glycogen in muscles is generally greater.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best represents system software?

options.text: Software used to design custom projects
Software that controls all internal computer functions

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Software that controls all internal computer functions'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **System Software:**

 
 
• System software is a type of computer program that is designed to run a computer's hardware and application programs. If we think of the computer system as a layered model, the system software is the interface between the hardware and user applications.
 
• The main purpose of system software is to manage the resources of the computer, such as the central processing unit (CPU), memory, and peripheral devices like printers and scanners.
 
• The most prominent example of system software is the **Operating System (OS)**, which manages all other programs in a computer. Examples include Microsoft Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
 
• System software runs in the background and is responsible for essential tasks such as booting the computer, managing files, and ensuring that the hardware components communicate effectively with each other.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Application Software:**

 
 
• Unlike system software, application software (or "apps") is designed to perform specific tasks for the user. These programs run on top of the system software.
 
• **Software used for preparing presentations:** This refers to productivity software like Microsoft PowerPoint or Google Slides. These are application softwares used for specific creative or professional communication tasks.
 
• **Software used to play games:** Video games are a category of application software designed for entertainment. They utilize the resources managed by the system software to render graphics and process user input.
 
• **Software used to design custom projects:** Programs like Adobe Photoshop, AutoCAD, or specialized project management tools are application softwares tailored for specific professional outputs and user-driven projects.
 
 
 
• **Utility Software:**
 
 
• Often considered a sub-type of system software, utility software helps analyze, configure, optimize, or maintain a computer. Examples include antivirus programs, disk defragmenters, and file compression tools.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• System software is generally written in low-level programming languages (like C or Assembly) to interact directly with the hardware with maximum efficiency.
 
• Without system software, a computer would be a collection of useless hardware parts; it provides the platform necessary for any application software to function.
 
• Device drivers are also a crucial part of system software, acting as translators between the operating system and specific hardware devices like printers or graphic cards.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Alt + Tab keyboard shortcut in Windows?

options.text: To close the currently active window

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'To switch between open windows'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alt + Tab (Task Switcher):**

 
 
• The Alt + Tab shortcut is one of the most fundamental multitasking features in the Microsoft Windows operating system.
 
• It allows users to quickly toggle between active software applications and open windows without using a mouse.
 
• When the Alt key is held and the Tab key is pressed, a graphical overlay appears on the screen showing thumbnails or icons of all running programs.
 
• Continuing to tap the Tab key while holding Alt moves the selection box forward through the open windows, and releasing the Alt key brings the selected window to the foreground.
 
• This functionality is essential for professional workflows, enabling a seamless transition between different tasks, such as referencing a web browser while typing in a document.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To open Task Manager:**

 
 
• The direct keyboard shortcut to open the Task Manager in Windows is **Ctrl + Shift + Esc**.
 
• Alternatively, **Ctrl + Alt + Delete** can be used to access a security screen that includes a link to the Task Manager. It is primarily used to monitor system resources or terminate unresponsive processes.
 
 
 
• **To minimize all open applications:**
 
 
• The primary shortcut to clear the screen and show the desktop is **Windows Key + D**.
 
• Another common shortcut is **Windows Key + M**, which specifically sends all windows to the taskbar.
 
 
 
• **To close the currently active window:**
 
 
• The standard keyboard shortcut to exit an active application or close a window is **Alt + F4**.
 
• If used while on the desktop with no programs active, it typically brings up the Windows Shutdown dialog box.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Alt + Shift + Tab:** Holding the Shift key while using the Alt + Tab sequence allows the user to cycle through the open windows in **reverse order**.
 
• **Windows + Tab:** This shortcut opens the **Task View**, which provides a full-screen overview of all open windows and allows for the management of virtual desktops.
 
• **Ctrl + Alt + Tab:** This variation opens the task switcher and keeps it on the screen even after the keys are released, allowing the user to use arrow keys to select a window.
 
• Alt + Tab has been a staple feature of Windows since **Windows 3.0**, though its visual interface has evolved significantly with each version of the OS.

The given expression is in the standard identity form: (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).

This algebraic identity always simplifies to (a + b + c).

Required Value = 2.33 + 1.55 + 1.22 = 5.1.

**∴ Answer = 5.1**

questions.question: Which of the following thickens sauces and soups due to its ability to absorb water and form a gel?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Starch'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Starch:**

 
 
• Starch is a complex carbohydrate found in plants like corn, potatoes, wheat, and rice. It is the most common thickening agent used in culinary arts for making sauces, soups, and gravies.
 
• The process by which starch thickens a liquid is known as **gelatinization**. When starch granules are heated in a liquid, they absorb water and swell significantly.
 
• As the temperature increases, the starch granules eventually burst, releasing starch molecules (amylose and amylopectin) into the liquid. These molecules form a network that traps water, resulting in a thickened, viscous consistency or a gel.
 
• Starches are preferred for thickening because they are relatively flavorless, effective in small quantities, and provide a smooth, glossy texture to the final dish.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sugar:**

 
 
• While sugar can increase the viscosity of a liquid when used in very high concentrations (creating a syrup), it does not "absorb" water to form a gel structure like starch does.
 
• Sugar is primarily used as a sweetener and a preservative. In baking, it helps with browning (caramelization) and moisture retention, but it is not a standard thickening agent for savory soups or sauces.
 
 
 
• **Oil:**
 
 
• Oil is a fat and is hydrophobic, meaning it does not mix with or absorb water.
 
• While oil can be part of a thickening process (such as in a **roux**, where it is cooked with flour), oil alone will float on top of a liquid rather than thickening it into a gel. In emulsions like mayonnaise, oil is suspended in water, but it does not function through water absorption.
 
 
 
• **Salt:**
 
 
• Salt is a mineral primarily used for seasoning, enhancing flavor, and preservation.
 
• Salt does not have the molecular structure required to form a gel or thicken liquids. In fact, salt can sometimes inhibit the thickening power of certain starches if added in excessive amounts during the early stages of cooking.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The temperature at which gelatinization occurs varies depending on the type of starch; for example, **cornstarch** typically thickens between 144°F and 162°F (62°C to 72°C).
 
• **Slurry:** A common method to add starch to a hot soup is by creating a slurry (mixing starch with a cold liquid first) to prevent lumps from forming.
 
• **Retrogradation:** This occurs when a starch-thickened sauce cools down and the starch molecules rearrange into a more crystalline structure, sometimes causing the liquid to "weep" or separate (syneresis).
 
• Common culinary thickeners derived from starch include **all-purpose flour, arrowroot, tapioca, and potato starch**.

questions.question: The Constitution (Ninety‑Fifth Amendment) Act of 2009 extended the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo‑Indians for how many years?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Ten Years'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Constitution (Ninety-Fifth Amendment) Act, 2009:**

 
 
• The 95th Amendment Act specifically amended **Article 334** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It extended the period of reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• It also extended the period for the **special representation of the Anglo-Indian community** by nomination for another **ten years**.
 
• Before this amendment, the reservation was set to expire on January 25, 2010 (60 years from the commencement of the Constitution). This act extended it to **January 25, 2020 (70 years)**.
 
• The primary objective was to ensure that the underprivileged sections of society continued to have a voice in the legislative process until their socio-economic conditions improved further.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Twenty Years:**

 
 
• While the total duration of reservation has been extended multiple times, the 95th Amendment specifically added a 10-year increment to the existing 60-year limit.
 
• Historically, the 8th Amendment (1960) was the first to extend the original 10-year limit to 20 years, but it is not the duration associated with the 2009 Act.
 
 
 
• **Fifteen Years:**
 
 
• There is no constitutional amendment regarding Article 334 that extended the political reservation for a specific block of fifteen years. Extensions have traditionally been granted in 10-year intervals.
 
 
 
• **Five Years:**
 
 
• A five-year term usually refers to the tenure of the Lok Sabha or State Assemblies, but it has not been the standard duration for extending constitutional reservations for SC/STs under Article 334.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Article 334:** This article originally provided that the reservation of seats and special representation would cease 10 years after the commencement of the Constitution (i.e., in 1960).
 
• **Subsequent Extensions:** Through various amendments (8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, and 95th), this period was consistently extended every 10 years.
 
• **104th Amendment Act (2019):** This is the most recent amendment related to this topic. It extended the reservation for SCs and STs for another **ten years** (until January 25, 2030).
 
• **Anglo-Indian Representation:** Importantly, the **104th Amendment Act did not extend** the reservation for the Anglo-Indian community, effectively ending their nomination process in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies as of January 2020.

questions.question: A shopkeeper professes to sell his goods at a 35% loss but uses a false balance and gains 55%. The actual weight (rounded off to one decimal place) he uses instead of 1 kg is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit Ratio = 155 ÷ 100 (for 55% gain)

Price Multiplier = 65 ÷ 100 (for 35% loss)

False Weight = True Weight × (Price Multiplier ÷ Net Profit Ratio)

Actual Weight = 1000 × (65 ÷ 155) = 65000 ÷ 155

Actual Weight ≈ 419.35 gm

**∴ Answer = 419.4 gm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Professed Loss = 35%, Overall Gain = 55%, True Weight = 1000 gm

**Formula used:**

(100 + Gain%) ÷ (100 − Professed Loss%) = True Weight ÷ False Weight

 True Weight (1000 gm) 
• False Weight (x gm) 
 Weight Gap (Error) Loss Professed: 35% Actual Gain: 55% Result: x = 419.4 gm 

**Calculations:**

Let the weight used be x grams.

⇒ (100 + 55) ÷ (100 − 35) = 1000 ÷ x

⇒ 155 ÷ 65 = 1000 ÷ x

⇒ x = (1000 × 65) ÷ 155

⇒ x = 65000 ÷ 155

⇒ x = 419.3548... ≈ 419.4 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 419.4 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Dishonest Dealer Profit

When a dealer sells at cost price but uses a false weight, Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Combined Dishonest Dealer Formula

If a dealer professes k% profit and uses false weight, then Overall Profit% = [(100 + k) × (True Weight ÷ False Weight) − 100].

False Balance Multiplication

If the weight is faulty by x% while buying and y% while selling, Total Gain% = [((100+x)(100+y) ÷ 100) − 100].

questions.question: Which centrally sponsored scheme aims to create community infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas (MCAs) to address development deficits, as stated by Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS in July 2025?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS)

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK)'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK):**

 
 
• PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) implemented by the Ministry of Minority Affairs to address development deficits in identified Minority Concentration Areas (MCAs).
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the socio-economic conditions of the minorities and provide basic amenities to them for improving their quality of life and reducing imbalances in the identified MCAs.
 
• The scheme focuses on creating community infrastructure in priority sectors such as Education, Health, Skill Development, and Women Empowerment.
 
• Infrastructure projects include the construction of school buildings, hostels, smart classrooms, ITIs, polytechnics, health centers, and Sadbhav Mandaps (community centers).
 
• The MCAs are identified based on the concentration of minority populations and their relative backwardness in terms of socio-economic and basic amenity parameters.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS):**

 
 
• PM VIKAS is an integrated scheme that umbrellas five erstwhile schemes of the Ministry: Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, and Nai Manzil.
 
• It focuses on the skilling, entrepreneurship, and leadership training requirements of the minority communities, particularly the artisan communities.
 
• The aim is to improve the livelihoods of minorities through capability building and market linkages.
 
 
 
• **Padho Pardesh:**
 
 
• This was a scheme that provided interest subsidies on educational loans for overseas studies to students belonging to economically weaker sections of notified minority communities.
 
• The focus was specifically on financial aid for higher education abroad, rather than physical community infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Seekho Aur Kamao:**
 
 
• This is a placement-linked skill development scheme for minorities.
 
• It aims to upgrade the skills of minority youth in various modern/traditional skills depending upon their educational qualification, present economic trends, and market potential.
 
• The goal is to ensure they obtain suitable employment or become self-employed.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• PMJVK was evolved from the erstwhile **Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP)**, which was launched in 2008-09.
 
• The scheme has been restructured to increase its reach and effectiveness, covering all districts of the country where Minority Concentration Areas are identified.
 
• The funding pattern for PMJVK is generally **60:40** between the Centre and States, and **90:10** for North Eastern and Himalayan States.
 
• Central assistance is provided to the State Governments/UT Administrations for the implementation of the projects approved by the Ministry.

questions.question: If 5³x ⁺ ⁴ = (5 ⁴)¹⁰⁵ , then find the integral part of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the exponents on both sides of base 5.

Exponent on RHS = 4 × 105 = 420.

Equate with LHS exponent: 3x + 4 = 420.

3x = 416 → x = 138.66...

The integral part is the value before the decimal.

**∴ Answer = 138**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation: 5³x ⁺ ⁴ = (5⁴)¹⁰⁵

**Formula used:**

(am)ⁿ = am × ⁿ

If ap = aq, then p = q (where a > 0, a ≠ 1)

 LHS 5³x ⁺ ⁴ = RHS (5⁴)¹⁰⁵ 
• 
• 3x + 4 = 4 × 105

**Calculations:**

5³x ⁺ ⁴ = 5⁴ × ¹⁰⁵

⇒ 5³x ⁺ ⁴ = 5⁴²⁰

⇒ 3x + 4 = 420

⇒ 3x = 420 − 4

⇒ 3x = 416

⇒ x = 416 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 138.666...

The integral part of a number is the greatest integer less than or equal to that number.

⇒ Integral part of x = 138

**∴ The correct answer is 138.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product and Quotient Laws of Indices

When bases are the same, multiply by adding powers: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ. Divide by subtracting powers: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ.

Integral Part (Greatest Integer Function)

The integral part of a real number x, often denoted as [x], is the largest integer that is not greater than x. For example, [138.66] = 138.

Power of a Power Rule

When a base with an exponent is raised to another power, multiply the exponents together: (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ.

Negative and Zero Indices

Any non-zero base raised to the power of 0 equals 1 (a⁰ = 1). A negative power indicates a reciprocal: a−ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle, if the lengths of the opposite side and the adjacent side to angle θ are 7 cm and 21 cm, respectively, then what is the value of tanθ?

The tangent ratio tanθ in a right-angled triangle is always defined as the ratio of the side opposite to the angle to the side adjacent to it.

tanθ = Opposite Side ÷ Adjacent Side

tanθ = 7 ÷ 21 = 1/3

**∴ Answer = 1/3**

**Given:**

Length of the opposite side = 7 cm

Length of the adjacent side = 21 cm

**Formula used:**

tanθ = Perpendicular / Base = Opposite Side / Adjacent Side

 
 
• 
• Opposite (7) Adjacent (21) θ Right-Angled Triangle 

**Calculations:**

We know the trigonometric ratio for tangent is:

⇒ tanθ = Opposite Side / Adjacent Side

⇒ tanθ = 7 / 21

⇒ tanθ = 1 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

In any right triangle: sinθ = Opposite/Hypotenuse, cosθ = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, and tanθ = Opposite/Adjacent.

Pythagoras Theorem

The hypotenuse H can be found using H² = Opposite² + Adjacent². Here, H = √(7² + 21²).

Reciprocal Identities

The reciprocal of tangent is cotangent: cotθ = 1/tanθ = Adjacent/Opposite. For this problem, cotθ = 21/7 = 3.

questions.question: Who made history in November 2025 as the first Muslim and South Asian American elected Lieutenant Governor of Virginia?
questions.solution:

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghazala Hashmi:**

 
 
• In November 2025, Ghazala Hashmi made history by becoming the first Muslim and the first South Asian American to be elected as the Lieutenant Governor of Virginia.
 
• She previously served as a member of the Virginia Senate, representing the 15th district, where she was also the first Muslim woman elected to that body in 2019.
